packet.body_excerpt:
Core schemas of completed models are stored — and thus shared — when embedded in referencing schemas, so the structure traversed during schema cleaning is a DAG, not a tree. `gather_schemas_for_cleaning()` traversed it once per *path*, which is exponential in the number of interconnected models: in a chain of models each referencing the previous three, a single model class 25 levels deep took 16 seconds to create, and a 300-model chain could not finish building at all. For `google.genai` (766 models), roughly 8× more schema nodes were walked than exist.

Each schema object is now traversed only once. To preserve the per-encounter semantics of the definition reference counting, the references encountered within a schema's traversal span are marked as non-inlinable when the schema object is reached again — including while its traversal is still in progress, which would otherwise inline a definition into a reference reachable from that same definition and create a cyclic schema.

The 300-model chain above now builds in under a second; the added regression test would effectively never finish without this change.

~~A second commit makes `FieldInfo._qualifiers` use a shared empty `frozenset` (the attribute is only ever read, and a per-field empty `set` costs 216 bytes).~~

packet.objective: Avoid exponential core schema traversal in `gather_schemas_for_cleaning()`

acceptance: Each schema object is visited once even when several paths reach it
Definition reference counting keeps its per-encounter semantics
Creating chains of interconnected models completes in linear time
ruling.objective: Traverse each core schema object once in gather_schemas_for_cleaning(), so schema cleaning is linear in the number of schemas rather than exponential in the number of paths
ruling.rationale: Performance fix that visits each schema object once; the PR body explains how per-encounter reference counting is preserved and the diff carries a regression test. Nothing referenced it afterwards.
